title: Cop believes accused killer 'honest'
subtitle: Never aimed to kill, Sand told police
article: An RCMP interrogator has testified that he believed Robert Sand's claim that he never aimed his gun at RCMP Const. Dennis Strongquill, but was instead firing at Strongquill's cruiser.
"I felt he was being honest," said Cpl. Joe Nowell in court Tuesday. "But exactly how much he was going to tell us I did not know."
Nowell and Cpl. Jim Atras took a statement from Robert Sand one day after Strongquill was shot dead on Dec. 21, 2001.
Sand, 24, and his lover Laurie Bell, 21, are charged with first- degree murder for his slaying.

In his cross-examination of Nowell, Sand's defence lawyer Greg Brodsky stressed that at no time in the statement did Robert Sand ever say he was firing at the police. Nowell agreed with Brodsky on this point.

Sand told police interrogators that a police car pulled over his truck on the highway outside of Russell, Man. His brother Danny was driving, Robert said, while Bell was sleeping in the back seat of their truck. Robert got out of his truck, carrying a loaded shotgun.
"I started shooting four rounds into the front of the vehicle," he told the interrogators.

When the police fled, Robert told his brother Danny to chase the police cruiser. In Russell, Danny is alleged to have rammed the cruiser, while Robert fired into it, killing Strongquill. In his statement, Robert said, "I emptied six more rounds, I think, to the side of the police vehicle."
During the altercation, Strongquill's partner Const. Brian Auger fired a number of shots at the Sands, wounding Danny.

Robert spoke in his statement as if he saw only one police officer in the RCMP cruiser, not two. "He (the officer) was shooting. I could hear breaking glass, metal tearing... And I just remember shooting -- shooting at the fire from his truck." Robert said he didn't know a police officer was dead after the gunfight, according to the statement.
As the threesome were being chased by RCMP across Saskatchewan, Robert said he fired again at a pursuing cruiser. "I shot at the front end of his vehicle, to try and disable it."
At the end of the police interview, both Atras and Nowell told Robert they felt he was being truthful.
"Well, I think you've been very honest," Nowell said.
At the time, both officers had only sketchy details of the crime and crime scene.
